samples.summary: The frontend copy of the CRDT read boundary (`normalizeListLevel(Number(attrs.listLevel))`) has no test; only the docs-engine twin is covered
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts:210-223` exercises the engine's `treeNodeToBlock` clamp ('the CRDT read boundary clamps a peer-supplied level'), but the module the live collaborative editor actually reads through is `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`'s own private `treeNodeToBlock` (line 493-502). Greps for `normalizeListLevel|MAX_LIST_LEVEL` across the repo return no frontend test hit, and greps for `not-a-number|listLevel.*NaN|Number.isFinite` in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs` return only the block-style guard test (`yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2637-2672`), which poisons `lineHeight`/`marginTop`/`textIndent` but not `listLevel`. That file already has the exact fixture pattern needed (a `yorkie.Tree` with string attributes), so the omission is coverage, not infeasibility. samples.summary: The text-box editor's new `doc.batch()` wrapping (one undo unit for a subtree move) is not asserted anywhere
samples.evidence: The docs editor gets a dedicated `TracingStore` suite ('a list level gesture is one undo unit', `editor-tab-bullet.test.ts`) asserting `writeDepths === [1,1]` and `canUndo() === false` after one undo. The text-box counterpart's only new test (`packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:544-585`) asserts committed `listLevel`s after indent/outdent/indent and never touches batching or undo, so removing `doc.batch(...)` from `text-box-editor.ts` indent/outdent would leave the suite green while a Slides/Board user's Cmd+Z half-moves the subtree.

samples.summary: The cursor-flush tests only record the batch depth of `setCursorForHistory`; nothing asserts the pre-edit caret/selection is actually what gets flushed
samples.evidence: `TracingStore.setCursorForHistory(): void` takes no parameters and pushes only `this.depth`, and the two tests assert `cursorFlushDepths[0] === 0`. So the ordering claim is covered, but a regression that flushes the *post-edit* caret, or passes `null` selection where a range existed (#523's actual symptom), still passes. The real `YorkieDocStore.setCursorForHistory` is never involved in any test of this path.

samples.summary: No test covers whether the toolbar `indent()`/`outdent()` paths flush the pre-edit caret for history (they call `docStore.snapshot()` directly, bypassing `recordCursorForHistory`)
samples.evidence: `editor.ts` indent/outdent call `docStore.snapshot()` inside `doc.batch(...)` and never call `recordCursorForHistory`, while the Tab/Cmd+] paths in `text-editor.ts` do call it before the batch. The 'the toolbar path batches its writes too' test asserts only `writeDepths === [1,1]` and never inspects `cursorFlushDepths`, so the asymmetry (undo restoring a stale caret after a toolbar indent) is unobserved either way.

finding.summary: The frontend copy of the CRDT read boundary (`normalizeListLevel(Number(attrs.listLevel))`) has no test; only the docs-engine twin is covered
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts:210-223` exercises the engine's `treeNodeToBlock` clamp ('the CRDT read boundary clamps a peer-supplied level'), but the module the live collaborative editor actually reads through is `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`'s own private `treeNodeToBlock` (line 493-502). Greps for `normalizeListLevel|MAX_LIST_LEVEL` across the repo return no frontend test hit, and greps for `not-a-number|listLevel.*NaN|Number.isFinite` in `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs` return only the block-style guard test (`yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2637-2672`), which poisons `lineHeight`/`marginTop`/`textIndent` but not `listLevel`. That file already has the exact fixture pattern needed (a `yorkie.Tree` with string attributes), so the omission is coverage, not infeasibility. If this clamp regresses or is dropped, a peer writing `listLevel: 'NaN'`/`'1e9'` reaches `computeListCounters` (`RangeError`) and the layout indent in the real app and no suite fails.

verdict.reason: The absence itself checks out — no frontend test poisons `listLevel` (the sole `attributes: {… listLevel …}` fixture repo-wide is the engine's, packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts:214; the frontend poisoned-attrs test at yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2637-2672 covers only style fields, and the other frontend `yorkie.Tree` fixtures and the concurrent integration suite never poison it). But the finding's major grading rests on a counterfactual the repo contradicts: the frontend store's clamp (yorkie-doc-store.ts:501) is redundant defense-in-depth, not the last line. Every reader named in the evidence normalizes at point of use — layout.ts:1097 (computeListCounters) and :497 (indent), pdf-painter.ts:370,593, markdown.ts:145, list-level.ts:50 (planner) — and those point-of-use guards are tested (list-level.test.ts:225-240, :242-251) alongside the helper's band (list-level.test.ts:172-197). The frontend renders through that engine (docs-view.tsx:1-7 `initialize` from @wafflebase/docs) and no frontend code outside the store consumes `block.listLevel` (only type decls in text-formatting/types.ts:61,78). So dropping line 501 would yield no RangeError, no layout corruption, and no user-visible or data-affecting defect — the gap is a duplicated repair with contained failure while the clamp semantics are covered, i.e. minor, not a blocking major.

No test asserts that one indent/outdent gesture is a single undo unit, though wrapping in `doc.batch()` is a headline behavior change of this diff

finding.summary: The diff's headline structural change — wrapping indent/outdent in `doc.batch()` so a multi-block subtree move is ONE undo unit — has no test in any of the three editors
finding.evidence: editor.ts, text-editor.ts and text-box-editor.ts all gained `doc.batch(() => { snapshot(); applyListLevelChanges(...); ... })` with long comments claiming "one Cmd+Z would leave the subtree half-moved" without it. No added test presses undo. `grep -n undo packages/docs/test` returns hits in memory.test.ts, editor-page-setup.test.ts ('a page-setup change is one undo step'), table-cell-style-guard.test.ts, text-box-editor.test.ts:351 ('exposes undo and redo' — only asserts typeof/not.toThrow) — none over indent/outdent. The seam is demonstrably testable (editor-page-setup.test.ts:159 does exactly this pattern with `editor.undo()`), so nothing prevents a regression that drops or misplaces the batch: a user's Cmd+Z would then leave a list subtree half-moved, and under Yorkie a peer would observe the parent-at-child-level state the change exists to remove.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is contradicted by the very file the finding names. packages/docs/test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts:713 opens a describe block titled 'a list level gesture is one undo unit', devoted to the batch change. Two tests press undo: :763 'one undo puts the whole subtree back, and there is nothing after it' presses Tab, calls editor.undo() at :769, asserts the full subtree reverts ([1,2,0] -> [0,1,0]) and that store.canUndo() is false at :775 (exactly the single-undo-unit property); :779 does the same for Shift+Tab (undo at :795, canUndo false at :798). Three further tests (:752, :802, :812) assert store.writeDepths toEqual([1,1]) for the keyboard Tab, Cmd+], and toolbar indent()/outdent() paths, so both subtree writes must be issued inside an open batch — dropping or misplacing doc.batch() yields [0,0] and fails. :827 and :840 additionally pin the pre-edit cursor flush to depth 0, i.e. outside the batch. The coverage is not over-mocked: no vi.mock in the file (imports at :2-6), TracingStore (:675) extends the real MemDocStore and delegates via super.batch/super.setBlockType (:686, :698) recording only depth, and the editor is the real initialize() editor (:739) driven by dispatched keydown events. The instrumented seam matches production: editor.ts:3608 and :3627 wrap docStore.snapshot() + applyListLevelChanges(+/-1) in doc.batch(), with applyListLevelChanges documenting the batch requirement at :1595. As an absence claim, this single counterexample settles it regardless of the other two editors.
